description: Non-hormonal treatment options for menopause symptoms

entries.title: Fezolinetant (Veozah)
entries.description: FDA-approved non-hormonal medication for hot flashes
entries.content: Fezolinetant (brand name Veozah) is a groundbreaking non-hormonal medication FDA-approved in 2023 specifically for treating moderate to severe hot flashes associated with menopause. It works as a neurokinin 3 (NK3) receptor antagonist, blocking specific brain pathways that trigger hot flashes and regulate body temperature. This represents a major advancement for women who cannot or choose not to use hormone therapy.
entries.mechanism: Blocks NK3 receptors in the brain's thermoregulatory center
entries.effectiveness: Significantly reduces frequency and severity of hot flashes; improves sleep quality and quality of life
entries.who_can_use: Women with moderate to severe hot flashes who cannot or prefer not to use hormone therapy
benefits: Improves sleep disrupted by night sweats
side_effects: May worsen sleep problems in some women
entries.monitoring: Liver function tests required before starting and periodically during treatment
entries.when_to_see_doctor: Discuss if you have moderate to severe hot flashes and want a non-hormonal option

entries.title: SSRIs and SNRIs (Antidepressants)
entries.description: Certain antidepressants that can reduce hot flashes and help mood symptoms
entries.content: Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors (SSRIs) and Serotonin-Norepinephrine Reuptake Inhibitors (SNRIs) are antidepressants that can help manage both hot flashes and mood symptoms during menopause. Low-dose paroxetine (Brisdelle) is FDA-approved specifically for hot flashes. These medications are particularly useful for women who cannot take hormone therapy or who also have depression or anxiety.
examples: Paroxetine (Paxil, Brisdelle) - FDA approved for hot flashes
entries.effectiveness: Moderate - reduces hot flashes by 40-60%; also helps mood symptoms
entries.who_can_use: Women with hot flashes and/or mood symptoms, especially those who cannot use HRT
benefits: Reduces hot flash frequency and severity
side_effects: Sexual side effects (reduced libido, difficulty orgasming)
important_notes: Takes 2-4 weeks to see full effect
Some SSRIs can interfere with tamoxifen (breast cancer medication)
entries.when_to_see_doctor: Discuss if you have hot flashes and/or mood symptoms

entries.title: Gabapentin (Neurontin, Gralise)
entries.description: Anti-seizure medication effective for hot flashes, especially at night
entries.content: Gabapentin is an anti-seizure medication that has been shown to reduce hot flashes, particularly nighttime hot flashes and night sweats. It's especially useful for women who cannot take estrogen therapy or who have severe nighttime symptoms disrupting sleep.
entries.form: Oral pills, typically taken at bedtime for nighttime symptoms or 2-3 times daily
entries.effectiveness: Moderate - reduces hot flashes by 40-50%, particularly effective for nighttime symptoms
entries.who_can_use: Women with hot flashes who cannot use HRT; particularly helpful for nighttime symptoms
benefits: Reduces hot flashes, especially at night
May help with pain and restless legs
entries.dosing_notes: Often started at low dose and gradually increased; bedtime dosing can minimize daytime drowsiness
entries.when_to_see_doctor: Discuss if hot flashes are severe, especially at night

entries.title: Clonidine (Catapres)
entries.description: Blood pressure medication that can reduce hot flashes
entries.content: Clonidine is a medication primarily used to treat high blood pressure, but it can also provide some relief from hot flashes. It's available as pills or patches. While it can help, it's not as commonly prescribed as other options due to potential side effects.
entries.who_can_use: Women with hot flashes who cannot use HRT, especially those with high blood pressure
benefits: Also treats high blood pressure if present
entries.limitations: Less effective than HRT or newer non-hormonal options; side effects can be limiting
entries.when_to_see_doctor: Discuss if other options haven't worked or you have high blood pressure

entries.title: Oxybutynin (Oxytrol)
entries.description: Overactive bladder medication that can help with hot flashes
entries.content: Oxybutynin is primarily used to treat overactive bladder and urinary incontinence, but it has also been shown to relieve hot flashes and night sweats. However, in older adults it may be linked to cognitive decline, so it should be used with caution.
entries.effectiveness: Moderate for hot flashes; effective for urinary symptoms
entries.who_can_use: Women with both hot flashes and urinary symptoms; use with caution in older adults
side_effects: Cognitive effects (memory, confusion) - especially in older adults
entries.cautions: May be linked to cognitive decline in older adults; use with caution
entries.when_to_see_doctor: Discuss if you have both hot flashes and urinary symptoms

entries.title: Vaginal Moisturizers and Lubricants
entries.content: Vaginal moisturizers and lubricants are non-hormonal, over-the-counter products that can help relieve vaginal dryness and discomfort during sex. Moisturizers are used regularly (2-3 times per week) to maintain vaginal moisture, while lubricants are used during sexual activity.
types: Vaginal moisturizers (Replens, K-Y Liquibeads) - used regularly
Water-based lubricants (Astroglide, K-Y Jelly) - used during sex
Silicone-based lubricants (Sliquid) - longer-lasting, used during sex
entries.effectiveness: Helpful for mild to moderate vaginal dryness; may not be sufficient for severe symptoms
usage_tips: Use water-based lubricants with condoms (oil-based can damage condoms)
Apply moisturizers regularly, not just before sex
May need to try different products to find what works best
entries.limitations: May not be sufficient for severe vaginal atrophy; vaginal estrogen is more effective
entries.when_to_see_doctor: If symptoms persist despite OTC products, discuss vaginal estrogen

entries.title: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT)
entries.description: Talking therapy that helps manage menopause symptoms
entries.content: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) is a type of talking therapy that can help manage various menopause symptoms, including hot flashes, mood problems, anxiety, and sleep issues. CBT teaches coping strategies, helps change unhelpful thought patterns, and provides tools to manage symptoms. It's particularly effective for mood symptoms and can reduce the impact of hot flashes even if it doesn't eliminate them.
entries.effectiveness: Evidence-based for mood, anxiety, and sleep; helps reduce distress from hot flashes
entries.who_can_use: All women, particularly those with mood or anxiety symptoms
benefits: Can be used alongside other treatments
entries.access: Available through NHS talking therapies, private therapists, or online programs
entries.format: Individual or group sessions, in-person or online
entries.when_to_see_doctor: Can self-refer to NHS talking therapies or discuss with doctor

entries.title: Ospemifene (Osphena)
entries.description: Selective estrogen receptor modulator for painful intercourse
entries.content: Ospemifene is a selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) taken as a daily pill to treat painful intercourse (dyspareunia) caused by vaginal atrophy. It acts like estrogen on vaginal tissues but has different effects on other tissues. It's not suitable for women with a history of breast cancer or high breast cancer risk.
entries.effectiveness: Effective for vaginal dryness and painful intercourse
entries.who_can_use: Postmenopausal women with painful intercourse due to vaginal atrophy
who_should_avoid: Women with history of breast cancer
Women at high risk for breast cancer
History of blood clots or stroke
entries.when_to_see_doctor: Discuss if painful intercourse persists and you cannot use vaginal estrogen
